scope: Proposition 10.5 (Compact transverse graph) of the manuscript “Abundance after nonvanishing for compact Kähler fourfolds” (preprints/Abundance-after-nonvanishing-for-compact-Kahler-fourfolds-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 034 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 89b5dd1a939cd7a6), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 73. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Assume b > 0, and fix any t∗ ∈ T = Pb. There is a coordinate-power map ψ : T′ = Pb → T of degree r in each coordinate, with R = OT′ (1) and an actual identity Rr ≃ ψ∗OT (1), which is unbranched over t∗, and the following data. On a neighborhood of the compact graph Ξ = S ×T T′ ⊂ V × T′ there are the two full root covers and a projective resolution with smooth ambient source W . The graph cut H′ inside the reduced inverse section divisor is compact and reduced SNC of pure dimension dim V − 1, with finitely many globally smooth components. The projection p′ : W → T′ is a submersion near H′, and every nonempty closed component intersection is smooth and proper over T′, carrying the restriction of one Kähler form on a neighborhood of H′. Locally near every compact graph slice over w ∈ T′, the resolved ambient data, including their projection and full tautological divisor ideal, are isomorphic to an open restriction of the ordinary product b Z × U′ for a local root chart. There the cut is H♭ = H ×U U′, and its actual dualizing line is ωH♭ ≃ pr∗ H ωH ⊗ pr∗ U′ (ωU′ ⊗ ψ∗ ω−1 U ). (10.16)
